speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are experiencing sudden-onset lower back pain radiating down your leg; to begin my evaluation, have you noticed if this pain gets worse when you cough, sneeze, or bear down?

speaker: Patient
text: 26-year-old woman. The patient reports exercising in the gym several hours ago when she suddenly felt a sharp pain in her lower back. She describes the pain as radiating down the side of her leg and into her foot.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Lumbar Disc Herniation (likely L5-S1) with Sciatic Nerve Radiculopathy.

**Reasoning:** The patient is a young female with sudden-onset mechanical back pain after exercise, accompanied by radicular pain radiating to the foot. This clinical picture is classic for a disc herniation. While the initial question regarding cough/sneeze was standard to check for increased intradiscal pressure (positive straining test), the mechanism of injury and radiation pattern strongly support this diagnosis. I will not ask further questions as the history is sufficient for a provisional diagnosis, but I will request imaging to confirm the level and severity.

REQUEST IMAGES: Lumbar_Spine_MRI
